site_model.what_it_is: A website that generates illustrated personalised family storybooks.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Families wanting a custom story featuring their children and other loved ones.
site_model.value_proposition: Turns a family memory into a fully illustrated book preview, with printed hardcovers available.
main_tasks: Add family characters and a shared memory
Generate and read the storybook preview
Check the price of a printed hardcover
site_model.pricing_model: A free digital preview is advertised; the actual hardcover price is not yet shown.
trust_signals: A statement that printed hardcovers ship across the UK
site_model.fit_for_me: Very relevant for a personalised fifth-birthday present for Aarav, provided creation is quick and the delivered hardcover price is clear.

127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.
127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.observation: The StoryHearth homepage presents a personalised family storybook service, with prominent 'Proceed' and 'See pricing' buttons and links to pricing and login. The page also outlines a three-step process and says digital previews are free while printed hardcovers ship across the UK.
127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.think_aloud: This looks relevant straight away—I could make a birthday book starring Aarav. The first paragraph is far too corporate, but the three steps look simple. I need to log in first before I make it.

review.purpose: Explain the personalised storybook service and let visitors begin creation, view prices, or log in.
review.what_is_happening: The homepage is open on a phone-sized screen. It contains a large hero message, two prominent action buttons, pricing and login links, a three-step summary, testimonials, and footer information.
review.first_impression: The offer sounds lovely, and 'Proceed' is obvious. The first paragraph is jargon-heavy and takes up a lot of space, while the top links are squeezed awkwardly on my phone.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I want to log in and start making Aarav's book.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the 'Log in' button at the top is visible.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, 'Log in' clearly means signing into my account.

issues.title: Corporate jargon in the main description
issues.evidence: Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It sounds technical and vague rather than warm and personal, so I have to work out what will actually happen.
issues.fix: Replace it with a short plain-English line such as 'Turn a family memory into a one-of-a-kind illustrated storybook starring your child.'

issues.title: Top navigation is cramped on mobile
issues.evidence: 'How it works' wraps onto two lines and crowds the StoryHearth, Pricing, and Log in controls.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The links look squeezed together and harder to tap accurately with one thumb.
issues.fix: Use a compact mobile menu with adequately sized tap targets, or shorten the link to 'How it works' in a single line.

issues.title: Hero image lacks a useful description
issues.evidence: [image (no description) 342x440]
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The illustration is difficult to interpret because I cannot tell whether it shows the kind of personalised book I would get.
issues.fix: Add concise alt text describing the book or family-story product shown.

issues.title: Printed-book price is not visible on the homepage
issues.evidence: Only 'See pricing' and 'Free digital preview · Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK' are shown.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to know whether this fits our family budget before investing time in creating and checking a book.
issues.fix: Show a clear starting price for a hardcover, and clarify whether delivery is included.

positives: The orange 'Proceed' button is highly visible.
The three-step process makes the basic service understandable.
The free digital preview makes trying the service feel low risk.

127.0.0.1:8765/login.html | Welcome back.title: Log in – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/login.html | Welcome back.observation: The login page has fields for email and password, plus a prominent “Log in” button. I can see account, privacy, terms, and contact links, but no printed-book price.
127.0.0.1:8765/login.html | Welcome back.think_aloud: Straightforward enough. I can see the two boxes straight away, though the labels disappear when I tap them. I’ll use my account details and get straight on with the book.

review.purpose: Allow an existing customer to access their StoryHearth account.
review.what_is_happening: The page asks for an email address and password, then offers a large “Log in” button. It also provides links to account registration, privacy, terms, and contact.
review.first_impression: Simple and recognisable. The big button is easy to use with one thumb, although the fields have no permanent visible labels.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would enter my account details now.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the two input boxes and the large orange “Log in” button are immediately visible.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. The placeholders “Email” and “Password” and the button “Log in” match what I want to do, though the textbox controls themselves technically have no labels.

issues.title: Login fields have placeholder-only labels
issues.evidence: [5] textbox (no label) placeholder "Email" and [6] textbox (no label) placeholder "Password"
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The labels may disappear as soon as I type, which makes it harder to check that I used the right box and less accessible to assistive technology.
issues.fix: Give both textboxes persistent visible labels and programmatic label associations rather than relying only on placeholders.

issues.title: Navigation wraps awkwardly on the narrow phone screen
issues.evidence: The screenshot shows “How it works” split over two lines around the StoryHearth heading.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It looks cramped and makes the top of the page feel less polished.
issues.fix: Use a compact mobile header with a menu icon, or keep navigation labels on one line without wrapping.

issues.title: Footer text has very low contrast
issues.evidence: The pale footer links “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact” sit on a very light background.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can hardly read them, especially with only a few minutes and one free hand.
issues.fix: Use a darker text colour with at least WCAG AA contrast against the footer background.

positives: The orange “Log in” button is prominent and easy to tap.
The form is short, with only two fields.
The page clearly says “Welcome back” and explains that I am logging in.
Privacy, terms, and contact links are available.

127.0.0.1:8765/dashboard.html | Welcome.title: My books – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/dashboard.html | Welcome.observation: I’m on the “My books” dashboard after logging in. It confirms that my account has no books, but it also shows an unclear “profile sync incomplete” error with an orange warning. A prominent “+ Create a new book” button offers the next step.
127.0.0.1:8765/dashboard.html | Welcome.think_aloud: I’m in, and the big orange button is obvious. That profile sync error makes me a bit wary, though—does that mean my details won’t come through? I’ll try creating the book first.

review.purpose: Show the books attached to my account and provide a way to create another one.
review.what_is_happening: After a successful login, the dashboard greets me, says that I have no books yet, and displays a warning that profile synchronisation is incomplete. The main available action is “+ Create a new book.”
review.first_impression: The big orange button is easy to spot and the page is mostly uncluttered, but that raw error message makes me wonder whether the book will miss my family details.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes. I want to start the birthday book now, and the large orange button appears to be the main action.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes. “+ Create a new book” is immediately visible below the message that I have no books yet.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. It clearly says I can create a new book, which is exactly what I need.

issues.title: Raw technical sync error
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can’t tell what failed, whether my family details are affected, or whether I need to do something before continuing.
issues.fix: Replace the error code with plain language such as “Some saved profile details couldn’t be loaded. You can still create a book, or retry your profile.” Include a clear Retry option if action is needed.

issues.title: Navigation wraps awkwardly on a phone
issues.evidence: The header labels wrap into “How it works,” “My books,” and separate “Log out” lines.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It looks crowded and slightly broken on my small phone screen, though the main task is still clear.
issues.fix: Use a compact mobile header with a menu icon, or shorten the labels and lay them out in a clean single row with adequate spacing.

issues.title: Footer text has very low contrast
issues.evidence: “Privacy,” “Terms,” “Contact,” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear extremely faint.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can barely see these links, so they look disabled and are difficult to tap accurately.
issues.fix: Darken the footer text to meet WCAG contrast requirements and keep visible links distinguishable from non-link copyright text.

positives: The successful login is confirmed by “Welcome back, Demo.”
The empty state clearly says, “You have no books yet.”
The large orange “+ Create a new book” button makes the next step obvious.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the star of the story?
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.observation: The Create your book form asks who the main child is and who else will appear, with fields for the child's name, age, pronouns and appearance, plus another character's name and relationship. All fields are currently empty, while the Relationship dropdown misleadingly defaults to Grandparent.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.think_aloud: This is quick and easy to scan. I can put Aarav in and add Meera as his little sister, but the relationship box already says “Grandparent,” so I definitely need to change that.

review.purpose: Collect basic details about the child who will star in the story and another character in it.
review.what_is_happening: The form is ready for character details. The child's name and appearance boxes are empty, the age and pronouns still say Select…, and the other-character relationship defaults to Grandparent despite nobody having entered a name.
review.first_impression: It looks straightforward on my phone and I can see everything I need without reading much. The default “Grandparent” is a bit odd, but easy to spot and change.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would fill this in now because it is directly on the way to creating Aarav's birthday book.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the labelled name, age and pronoun fields, followed by the second-character name and relationship field, are prominent and easy to notice.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Who's the star of the story?” and “Who else is in the story?” clearly match what I want; the single “Relationship” label is less explicit but still understandable in context.

issues.title: Relationship defaults to Grandparent
issues.evidence: Control [11] displays “Grandparent” even though control [10], “Who else is in the story?”, is empty.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A pre-selected relationship could accidentally put Meera in the story as a grandparent if I tapped Next without checking it.
issues.fix: Default the Relationship dropdown to “Select relationship” or leave it blank, and require an explicit choice before continuing.

issues.title: Second-character relationship is not clearly scoped
issues.evidence: The standalone label “Relationship” appears directly below “Who else is in the story?”.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It is only clear from the form order that this relationship belongs to the second character.
issues.fix: Rename the label to “Relationship to [child]” or show it as a grouped question once the second character's name is entered.

positives: The main purpose is obvious from the heading “Who's the star of the story?”.
The fields are large enough to tap comfortably on a phone.
Optional appearance details are clearly marked optional.
The form avoids requesting a long block of information at this step.

later_issues.title: The companion character only asks for a name and relationship
later_issues.evidence: “Who else is in the story?” has only a textbox and “Relationship”; there are no fields for Meera’s appearance, age or pronouns.
later_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I know Meera is two, but the form may make her look generic unless I add those details somewhere else.
later_issues.fix: Add optional fields for the companion’s age, pronouns and appearance, or explain on the next step that they can be included later.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Your story.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Your story.observation: The story-details form asks for the setting, a special object, and the family memory. All three fields are empty, with Back and prominent orange Next buttons below them.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Your story.think_aloud: Good, this is quick—just three boxes. I’ll add Abbey Park, Rory, and the cloud-shape memory, then tap Next.

review.purpose: Collect the setting, meaningful object, and central family memory that the personalised book should include.
review.what_is_happening: The form has three empty fields labelled for where the story happens, a special object, and the memory or idea behind the story. Back and Next controls are visible.
review.first_impression: Straightforward and much better than a long form. I can do this quickly on my phone.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, this is exactly the information I came here to add.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the three large text boxes are immediately visible.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. 'Tell us the memory or idea behind your story' clearly matches what I want to write.

issues.title: Desktop navigation breaks into awkward fragments
issues.evidence: The header visibly shows “How it works,” “StoryHearth,” “Pricing,” “My books,” and “Log out” squeezed across multiple lines, with “How it works” wrapping into “How it works.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It looks broken on my narrow phone screen and makes me wonder whether I’m looking at the whole menu.
issues.fix: Use a compact menu button on small screens, or prevent navigation labels from wrapping and keep the logo and menu in separate rows.

issues.title: Footer links have very low contrast
issues.evidence: “Privacy,” “Terms,” and “Contact” are extremely pale against the footer background.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can barely see them, so they don't look reliably available or tappable.
issues.fix: Use a darker, WCAG-compliant text colour and maintain at least a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.

positives: There are only three relevant fields, so this suits my limited time.
Field labels and placeholders are specific and easy to scan.
Back and Next buttons are large and visually distinct.
The previous character details appear to have been accepted because the flow advanced to this step.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Choose the.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Choose the.observation: The screen asks me to choose a reading level and illustration style for Aarav’s book. The options are presented as large radio buttons, with Lexile 200L–500L and Watercolour currently selected.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Choose the.think_aloud: These choices are clear, but “Lexile” is jargon I don’t understand. For a five-year-old, I’d choose the easiest range, and the watercolour style looks lovely, so I’ll keep that and press Next.

review.purpose: Choose the reading difficulty and visual style used to generate the personalised storybook.
review.what_is_happening: I can select one reading level and one illustration style. The current selections are Lexile 200L–500L and “Watercolour — soft and dreamy,” with a large Next button.
review.first_impression: It looks neat and easy to scan, and the large choices work well on my phone. I’m not going to stop over the style, but “Lexile” is a bit technical for me.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I want Aarav’s book to suit a five-year-old and I’m ready to choose the easiest reading level.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the four reading-level radio buttons and three illustration-style buttons are immediately visible.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Partly. The illustration labels clearly match what I want, but “Lexile BR–200L” does not plainly tell me that this is easiest or best for a five-year-old.

issues.title: Reading-level options use unfamiliar jargon
issues.evidence: "Lexile BR–200L" and "Lexile 200L–500L"
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I know Aarav reads at age five, so I need to pick the right range quickly. I cannot tell from the numbers alone which one is easiest.
issues.fix: Add a plain-English description such as “Easiest — ages 4–6” and “Easy — ages 6–8,” while retaining the Lexile range as secondary information.

positives: The two decisions are clearly separated.
Large radio controls are easy to tap with one thumb.
The selected state is visible.
Watercolour is already selected, so there is no need to make another decision.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Add a photo.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Add a photo.observation: The final creation step offers an optional photo upload and has Back and “Create my book” buttons. No file is selected, so I can skip the photo and generate the book from the details already entered.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Add a photo.think_aloud: I’ll skip the photo because I don’t have a suitable one on this phone and I don’t want to delay his present. The big “Create my book” button is clear, although the navigation at the top looks cramped.

review.purpose: Allow the customer to add a child’s photo before generating the personalised storybook.
review.what_is_happening: This is the last step before generation. A photo can be uploaded, or the customer can continue without one using “Create my book.”
review.first_impression: Simple and quick. I can easily skip the photo, though the navigation is squashed and the upload control itself looks like an old desktop-style file picker.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try creating the book now because I have entered all the story details.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the large teal “Create my book” button stands out immediately.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Create my book” clearly says that it will generate the birthday book.

issues.title: Navigation is cramped on a phone
issues.evidence: The top links “How it works,” “Pricing,” “My books,” and “Log out” wrap into an uneven multi-line layout.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes the page look less polished and wastes vertical space on my small screen.
issues.fix: Use a compact mobile header with a menu button, or shorten and align the links on one row.

issues.title: Upload control is visually dated and lacks a nearby field label
issues.evidence: [30] is shown as “Choose file” and “No file chosen,” with no separate visible label attached to the control.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can understand it, but the small grey desktop-style control does not match the rest of the phone-friendly design.
issues.fix: Use a large, labelled mobile upload button and add accessible file-state and validation text.

positives: The heading clearly says “Add a photo (optional),” so I know I can continue without one.
The “Create my book” button is large, prominent, and clearly labelled.
A Back button is available, giving me some control before generating the book.

127.0.0.1:8765/book.html | The Magical A.title: Your storybook – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/book.html | The Magical A.observation: The book has been generated as a nine-page preview, currently showing page 1 of 9, the cover. The page identifies the illustration style as “Pop-art comic” and offers controls to turn the pages, regenerate the entire book for $4.99, or proceed to “Order hardcover.”
127.0.0.1:8765/book.html | The Magical A.think_aloud: It’s worked, and the cover is cute, but it says “Adventrue” and “Pop-art comic” even though I chose Watercolour. I need to read every page before deciding whether this is suitable for Aarav.

review.purpose: Preview the complete generated picture book and choose whether to regenerate it or order a printed hardcover.
review.what_is_happening: A nine-page book titled “The Magical Adventrue of Aarav” has been generated. Page 1 is displayed with next-page, regeneration, and hardcover-order controls.
review.first_impression: The cover is bright and simple enough for Aarav, but the title has an obvious typo and the style is “Pop-art comic” when I selected Watercolour, which makes me doubt the rest of the book.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I want to read all nine pages because this is meant to be Aarav’s birthday present.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the right-arrow button and “1 / 9” make the page navigation obvious.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: The arrow is understandable, though a clearer “Next page” label would be better on a phone.

issues.title: Generated style does not match my selected style
issues.evidence: I selected “Watercolour,” but the page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic”.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I chose Watercolour for a five-year-old’s book, and an unexplained mismatch makes me distrust the other choices I made.
issues.fix: Apply the selected Watercolour style and show a confirmation beside the style, such as “Watercolour selected.”

issues.title: Generated title contains a spelling error
issues.evidence: The heading and cover say “The Magical Adventrue of Aarav.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: This is a birthday present, so a prominent typo makes it feel cheap and not ready to print.
issues.fix: Correct the title to “Adventure” and provide an edit control before ordering.

issues.title: Regeneration fee uses unexplained dollar pricing
issues.evidence: “Regenerate entire book – $4.99”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am in the UK and need a clear total before agreeing to a charge; there is no explanation of what happens if I dislike the generated book.
issues.fix: Show the fee in GBP, clarify that it is one-off, and ask for confirmation before charging.

issues.title: No visible edit or save control for the generated book
issues.evidence: The only visible book controls are “‹,” “›,” “Regenerate entire book – $4.99,” and “Order hardcover.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: If one page is wrong, I may have to pay to regenerate everything or abandon the book.
issues.fix: Add clear “Edit details,” “Edit page,” and “Save” controls, and explain whether edits are free.

issues.title: Small page-navigation buttons on a phone
issues.evidence: The controls shown as [6] and [7] are compact arrow buttons beneath the book.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am using one thumb and I could easily tap the wrong tiny arrow.
issues.fix: Use at least 44 by 44 pixel targets and label them “Previous page” and “Next page.”

positives: The “1 / 9” counter makes the preview length clear.
The next-page arrow is visible without hunting through the page.
The cover is colourful, simple, and suitable-looking for a young child.
review.abandon_reason: I want to read all nine pages before judging it, although the typo and wrong illustration style have made me wary of ordering it.

127.0.0.1:8765/checkout.html | Checkout.title: Checkout – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/checkout.html | Checkout.observation: The checkout shows the generated hardcover, a countdown, and a total price of £45.97, including a pre-selected £7.99 premium gift wrap and £12.99 shipping and handling. Empty address and payment fields appear below, with the Pay now button off-screen.
127.0.0.1:8765/checkout.html | Checkout.think_aloud: There it is: £45.97 before I’ve even entered an address. I didn’t ask for premium gift wrap, but it’s already ticked, so I’m unchecking that now. I won’t enter any payment details.

review.purpose: Show the complete hardcover cost and collect delivery and payment information.
review.what_is_happening: The generated book is selected as a £24.99 hardcover. Premium gift wrap is pre-selected for £7.99, shipping and handling is £12.99, and the resulting total is £45.97. A price-reservation countdown is active, and empty delivery and card fields lead toward payment.
review.first_impression: I can finally see the real total, but £45.97 feels steep and the pre-ticked £7.99 gift wrap immediately makes me wary. The narrow layout also makes the header wrap awkwardly.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would uncheck the gift wrap to establish the price I actually want, but I would not proceed to payment yet.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the checked “Premium gift wrap” box is very noticeable directly beneath the book price.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: The label and separate £7.99 price are clear, but it should not have been selected by default.

issues.title: Premium gift wrap is pre-selected
issues.evidence: [6] checkbox "Premium gift wrap" (checked), £7.99
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I’m price-sensitive and dislike paying for something I didn’t choose. The default makes the £45.97 total feel deliberately inflated.
issues.fix: Make optional extras unchecked by default, show the resulting total immediately, and require an explicit choice.

issues.title: Artificial reservation countdown adds pressure
issues.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:57”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes me rush before I’ve even understood the delivery or checked the book quality.
issues.fix: Remove the countdown unless there is a genuine, documented reservation policy, and explain precisely what expires.

issues.title: Navigation is cramped on mobile
issues.evidence: The header visibly wraps “How it works,” “Pricing,” “My books,” and “Log out” across multiple uneven lines.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It looks messy on my phone and makes the links harder to scan or tap accurately.
issues.fix: Use a compact mobile navigation menu or stack the links into clean full-width rows with adequately sized tap targets.

issues.title: Delivery charge is not explained before checkout
issues.evidence: “Shipping & handling £12.99” with no destination, timing, or service explanation nearby.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can’t judge the value or whether the charge applies to my Leicester address from this information alone.
issues.fix: Label the service and estimated delivery time, and make clear whether the charge varies by destination.

positives: The full total is displayed before payment.
The hardcover price and each charge are shown as separate amounts.
The gift-wrap price is visible beside its checkbox, so the added cost is not hidden once I notice it.

later_issues.title: Unchecked gift wrap still shows a £7.99 charge
later_issues.evidence: The checkbox for "Premium gift wrap" is unchecked, but the line still displays "£7.99".
later_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I might think the checkbox did not work or that I am still being charged for gift wrap.
later_issues.fix: Show the gift-wrap line as £0.00 when unchecked, or remove the charge line and clearly state that it is not included.

later_issues.title: The hardcover title contains a spelling error
later_issues.evidence: The checkout heading says "Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Aarav".
later_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes the product look unfinished, and I’m already unsure whether the generated book is good enough to print.
later_issues.fix: Allow the title to be edited before checkout and correct the spelling before presenting the order summary.

inputs.value: Short black hair, big brown eyes, red dinosaur t-shirt

inputs.field: Who else is in the story?

inputs.value: Aarav's red toy dinosaur called Rory

inputs.field: Tell us the memory or idea behind your story
inputs.value: Aarav teaching his little sister Meera to find shapes in the clouds at the park near our house on his fifth birthday. I want Aarav to be the hero.

output_reactions.reaction: The cover is bright and recognisable, but “Adventrue” looks careless, and I’m annoyed that it ignored the Watercolour style I chose. I want to see every page before deciding whether it is worth keeping.

The story is usable and personal, but the title misspells “Adventure” as “Adventrue,” the final image doesn’t show Meera, Rory or the park, and the ending feels sparse. It also says “Pop-art comic” despite me choosing Watercolour, so I’m not impressed with the finished result.

final_summary: Reviewed the complete generated book and found the hardcover checkout total of £37.98 after removing premium gift wrap. Did not enter payment details or pay.

console_errors: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)
